findings.title: D9's equality property sets openPair on rows the presentation table leaves without it
findings.recommendation: D9's Equality bullet says openPair is `missing: X` exactly when, on an `invoked` slot, the launch's landed members hold the other class and not X. The presentation table (`The first review slot covers what the user invoked`) sets openPair on ONE row only: PAIR-OPEN with one member landed ABOVE the bound. Two states differ: one member landed at or below the bound (the table's third row presents the landed member's class and sets no openPair), and a pair ended by a walk of its landed member (the member is a single, there is no open pair). An oracle built to D9 would fail the engine on both, or an engine built to the oracle would set openPair the table forbids. State the invoked half of the equality as the table's first row: the live launch has exactly one member landed, above the bound, and the pair has not ended.

findings.title: Decision 1's stop-to-warning cascade misses the walk body's degradation line and the charter
findings.recommendation: Two sites still state the retired behaviour. (1) `src/core/templates/workflows/address-reviews.ts:503` reads 'An open blind pair (a reviewed gate reports openPair) → NOT a degradation case: the walk stops before triage'; task 5.1 names :345, :349, :502 and :1040 but not :503, so an apply that installs the new fence leaves the body contradicting it. Name :503 in task 5.1. (2) rc17a's charter (`orbit/architecture/clean-up-review-cycle.md:3052`) names the state set 'NO-LAUNCH, PAIR-OPEN, COMPLETE, BROKEN'; the refined-at-propose note records D2-D4 but not that BROKEN became ENDED and the walk's stop became a warning. Add both to the note.

findings.title: Two sentences still read a walk of a pair half as foreclosing, against the ENDED rule
findings.recommendation: The reason requirement's rationale says the walk 'writes a record between the two members, foreclosing the pair permanently and costing two further independent passes' (line 837); on an `invoked` slot a walk of the landed half now ENDS the pair and the walked half covers as a single, so no further pass is owed. And the invoked-slot requirement opens 'A pair, once launched, covers only when both members land, blind' (line 8), without the ended case. Scope the rationale to a `blind-pair` slot and add the ended case to line 8, so neither reads as contradicting the membership requirement.

findings.title: The oracle's event set and design D4 do not carry the membership rule the walk settled
findings.recommendation: The membership rule now reads members from the trail reader's ACCEPTED passes and ends a pair at a walk of its landed member, and freshness decides whether a member covers. D9's event set (passes, pair launches, walk records, the tie) has no rejected external return and no apply token, so exit (1)'s oracle cannot measure the rejected-return row or a stale member — the finding this walk entry resolved asked for both. Add both to D9 and task 6.1. Design D4 (line 83) also still restates the window as 'later than L and earlier than the mode's next launch', without the walk ending it; point D4 at D10 or at the requirement rather than restating it.
